preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner to call the rebase() function
rewardsPool address must be set (not address(0)) before calling rebase()

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call the rebase() function with a very large multiple value (e.g., 10^18 or higher). This will multiply rebaseMultiple to an extremely large number, causing all balanceOf() and transfer calculations to return 0 due to division by the large rebaseMultiple. This effectively halts all token transactions. The attack sequence is: 1) Ensure rewardsPool is set via setRewardsPool(), 2) Call rebase() with a large multiple value, 3) Verify transactions are blocked by attempting a transfer.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The GoldHunt token contract has a rebase mechanism controlled by the owner. The rebaseMultiple variable is used as a divisor in balanceOf(), totalSupply(), transfer(), and other ERC20 functions. The rebase() function allows the owner to multiply rebaseMultiple by any value. If the owner sets a very large multiple (e.g., 2e18), rebaseMultiple becomes so large that all balance calculations return 0 due to integer division, effectively freezing all token transfers. The oracle checks if rebaseMultiple > 1e18.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.startPrank(). 2. Set a rewardsPool address (required precondition for rebase()). 3. Call rebase() with a large multiple value (2e18) to multiply rebaseMultiple beyond 1e18. 4. Verify rebaseMultiple exceeds the threshold.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Define GoldHunt interface with necessary functions (owner, setRewardsPool, rebase, rebaseMultiple). 2. In setUp(), instantiate the target contract. 3. In testExploit(), get owner address and impersonate it. 4. Call setRewardsPool() with a non-zero address. 5. Call rebase() with multiple = 2e18. 6. Assert rebaseMultiple > 1e18.
